turns.user: Do I need a Mexican fishing license for a 1.5 day trip?
turns.text:
Short answer: it depends on whether the trip actually fishes in Mexican waters — and the trip listing (or the landing) is the place to confirm that.

Here's what the rules say (summary, last checked 2026-11-25; confirm before you go):
- If the trip fishes in Mexican waters, each angler needs an individual Mexican sport-fishing permit from CONAPESCA, bought online by day/week/month/year or "excursion" ([CONAPESCA](https://www.gob.mx/conapesca/documentos/conapesca-01-016-pesca-deportivo-recreativa)).
- You also need to be on the boat's INM passenger list with the immigration fee paid (the FMM), and you should carry your passport ([INM](https://www.gob.mx/inm/acciones-y-programas/sport-fishing-and-nautical-tourism)).
- Mexico bag limit is 10 fish/angler, max 5 of one species; dorado counts as 5 fish with a 2/day cap; billfish/sharks 1/day ([CONAPESCA](https://www.gob.mx/conapesca/documentos/conapesca-01-016-pesca-deportivo-recreativa)).

Most 1.5-day listings in my data note "MX permit extra" (not included in the fare) — a couple of examples so you can see how it's worded:

<trip-card>{"tripId": "1086116", "why": ["Listing docs note: MX permit extra — buy it yourself before departure", "Confirm with Seaforth whether this trip enters Mexican waters"]}</trip-card>

<trip-card>{"tripId": "hm-8b45a4-12041800", "why": ["H&M 1.5 day — listing doesn't specify docs; ask the landing whether a MX permit/passport is needed"]}</trip-card>

<trip-card>{"tripId": "1091063", "why": ["Listing docs note: passport not required; MX permit extra", "Confirm with Fisherman's Landing whether this trip fishes Mexican waters"]}</trip-card>

Bottom line: if the boat crosses the border you'll need the CONAPESCA permit (and FMM/passport setup) — call or check the landing's page for that exact trip to be sure.
